sections.title: A verb that needs -val/-vel
sections.content: kijön (literally "comes out") means "to get along" when paired with -val/-vel — kijövök valakivel is "I get along with someone". The person you get along with always takes -val/-vel, never a bare noun.

items.english: I get along well with Petra.

items.spanish: Nehezen jövök ki valakivel, aki mindig komoly.
items.english: I have a hard time getting along with someone who's always serious.

sections.content: jól ("well") and nehezen ("with difficulty") are the two words that show up constantly with kijön — jól kijövök vs. nehezen jövök ki covers most of what you'll want to say.
Once you've already named the person, swap them for vele ("with him/her") instead of repeating the name — Jól kijövök vele is exactly as natural as repeating Petrával.
